name: book-index-tiering
title: book-index.md gains a nano tier, and full-book loading stops being unconditional
outcome: book-index.md offers nano, mini, and full tiers for all 14 vendored books, with a 3-nano-minimum judgment-gated escalation rule; Review/Maintenance's mandatory 14-file security corpus load gets the same cheap-signal-before-expensive-read shape, opposite default bias, no vendoring.
done_when: books/README.md's manifest lists nano.md, mini.md, and full.md for each of the 14 books
book-index.md states the 3-nano-minimum, judgment-gated escalation rule, replacing the prior 1-primary-plus-1-companion cap for book loading
design-mode.md's Stage 1/3 grounding section and the architecture skill's Review/Maintenance corpus-to-book escalation both reference the new rule

SKILL.md's Review mode security corpus step reads the first ~30 lines of all 14 security files unconditionally, then reads a file's remainder in full unless its summary clearly rules out applicability, defaulting to full on ambiguity

min_work.derived_from: 1 district (skills), 2 colliding ADRs (ADR-0015, ADR-0017), 2 boundary rules (book-index.md's prior 1+1 cap, Review mode's mandatory-14-file security rule)

epics.outcome: book-index.md, books/README.md, design-mode.md, and SKILL.md's Review mode security corpus step all reflect ADR-0021's two escalation rules (book tiering, and the security corpus applicability read)

rounds.note: Folded in the security corpus applicability read after a live discussion of whether the mandatory 14-file security load deserved the same scrutiny as book loading; resolved with an opposite default bias (full-on-ambiguity, not skip-on-ambiguity).
